notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #11] OPEN ALPHA DEMO: Turn-Based Combat and Political Compass
notes.content:
[p]Hello comrades,[/p][p align="start"]With less than a week to go before [b]Gamescom 2025[/b], we’d like to open up a bit about the contents of the [b]playable demo[/b] we’ll be presenting at the Cologne fair.
[/p][p align="start"]We’d like to remind you that [b]this demo will then be released on Steam as an Open Alpha Demo[/b], preceded by a [b]short playtesting session[/b] that will take place exclusively on our [url="https://discord.gg/HjPTxkfbCw"]Discord[/url].
[/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/79a16e9fa1b5624c4123d15bbccf708f983ce90e.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/42bc088aa5a273b58050e1253b7ae086e0458fd9.png"][/img][/carousel][h2][b]POLITICAL COMPASS[/b][/h2][p]Forget dexterity, strength, and agility — in GLASSHOUSE, the [b]character progression system is made up of five ideologies[/b] that define language, attitude, and physical inclination.[/p][list][*][p align="start"][b][i]Feudcratism:[/i][/b][i] reasonableness and mediation[/i][/p][/*][*][p align="start"][b][i]Holisticism:[/i][/b][i] sensitivity and progressivism[/i][/p][/*][*][p align="start"][i][b]Anarchism:[/b] subversion and citizen rights culture[/i][/p][/*][*][p align="start"][b][i]Confeudcratism:[/i][/b][i] negotiation and liberal spirit[/i][/p][/*][*][p align="start"][b][i]Colonialism:[/i][/b][i] aggressiveness and conservative force[/i][/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]In the Open Alpha Demo, you’ll be able to assign [b]7 PoVs (Points of View)[/b] to one or more of these ideologies and create your own [b]Political Class[/b], which will always be defined and recognized by the system in the tag at the bottom left of the menu.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/27f02eab4275d92a404c5779251564de4f265d4e.gif"][/img]
The Political Class is the natural extension of the player’s way of thinking and acting; [b]Political Checks[/b] are dialogue/interaction lines accessible only to minds aligned with your class — [b]there are no dice rolls, and they're not guaranteed actions[/b]. Every [b]NPC[/b] has their own Political Compass, and it’s up to the player to decide whether or not to use their ideological tools to resolve a situation.[/p][p align="start"]The Political Compass is [b]flexible enough to allow for total ideological inconsistency[/b] — there are no boundaries or limits to “changing sides,” just like in real life.[/p][p align="start"]By completing quests or optional dialogues, you can earn new PoVs. There is no predetermined structure — [b]game progression is entirely tied to the player’s playstyle[/b], where every small interaction might conceal a fresh perspective that helps you better understand the complex world around you.


 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/0247c942298628e6ef556ff23ff920236eddb3fe.gif"][/img][/p][h2][b]TURN-BASED COMBAT[/b][/h2][p]Combat in GLASSHOUSE isn’t repetitive — [b]it’s a situation that only occurs when your choices fail[/b] (or if you simply prefer a more aggressive style). The enemies you encounter aren’t cannon fodder; they’re your co-workers, neighbors, or long-time rivals.[/p][p align="start"]The range of choices also extends to combat itself: [b]every encounter can be resolved physically or through speech[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/546a15e338b962c2e6875723379d4b3b87f02daf.gif"][/img][/p][h3][i]\[TALK - Action][/i][/h3][p]Each enemy has a Strong, Weak, and Neutral Point, defined by their Political Compass. The player can choose from [b]5 dialogue approaches[/b] (reasonable, sensitive, subversive, persuasive, and aggressive), each of [b]which scales based on their political build[/b].[/p][p align="start"]Once the player has chosen their dialogue approach, a d6 is rolled. If it hits a [b]Weak Poin[/b]t, the result is added to the difference between the player’s ideology and the enemy’s [b]\[1d6 + (PlayerColonialism - EnemyColonialism)][/b]. If striking a weak point reduces the enemy’s [b]Threat Bar (TH)[/b], their strong point sends a d6 back at the player, while the neutral point has no effect on either side. When the enemy’s [b]TH is lower than the player’s TH, the “force surrender” option becomes available[/b], allowing the player to roll another d6 to make the opponent lay down their arms.[/p][p align="start"]As a result, [b]it is possible to complete GLASSHOUSE without killing anyone[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/fbaeafa42f8bca8445cf2bec4f2cf44e0fdbec90.gif"][/img][/p][h3][i]\[ATTACK - Action][/i][/h3][p][b]Every weapon has its own dice[/b] and can be used to reduce an opponent’s [b]HP[/b] to zero; dice rolls can randomly be dodged by either side. If an [b]attack doesn’t scale with your stats[/b], switching weapons during combat can be useful to exploit an enemy’s weaknesses (did someone say armor?), though it comes at the cost of sacrificing a turn.[/p][p align="start"]The equipped weapon also affects the player’s TH: a more powerful weapon, such as an axe or [b]a shotgun, can start the fight with higher TH[/b], intimidating the enemy and reducing the number of rhetorical attacks needed to unlock the “Force Surrender” option.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/eff0279b4f335536fb23bc3256f2337377f68e10.gif"][/img][/p][h3][i]\[USE - Action][/i][/h3][p]From [b]healing items[/b] to artifacts of questionable effect, this option is the [b]wild card[/b] of the combat system.[/p][p align="start"]For a quick example, during exploration you might find [b]items capable of embarrassing or unsettling potential enemies[/b]; if the player decides to keep a handy blackmail letter in their inventory, they [b]could use it in combat to instantly halve the enemy’s TH[/b].

[/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/052540d8a2e6dc82481d5b2bd184e54f766a7c62.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/bc7da09ebc4bd37fa280c80184a07c920f8d7f6b.png"][/img][/carousel][p]
There’s still much more to say about Combat and the Skill System — from [b]secret combinations[/b] to [b]unexpected evolutions[/b] — but that’s all for this first iteration. We’re not trying to reinvent the wheel of the classic RPG, but we want to experiment and bring together mechanics that are traditionally kept separate.[/p][p align="start"][b]We want to take the risk of making mistakes[/b], with a heart independent from distant and muddled market logic. We hope you can appreciate our attempt.[/p][p align="start"][i]Thank you all, see you soon![/i]
[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director FLAT28 Collective[/i][/p]

notes.title: ALPHA DEMO playable at GAMESCOM 2025!
notes.content:
[p]Hello flatmates,

we promised you big news for this year and so, between terror and excitement, we're kicking off the dance with a major announcement: this year we'll be present at [b]GAMESCOM 2025[/b] with an [b]Alpha Demo[/b] of GLASSHOUSE!

No tricks, no deception -- it will be completely open and you can come try it live in Cologne, from [b]August 20th to 24th[/b].

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/0f0d410462ded51756d85d64f919f97063588ff2.png"][/img][/p][h2]
GLASSHOUSE - THE ALPHA DEMO[/h2][p]After roughly two years of silence since the Concept Demo, we're finally ready to show you [b]the first 30 minutes of ACT I[/b] of GLASSHOUSE. Much has changed since your last visit to Dormitory 73B and we can't wait to show you the progress we've made thanks to your feedback as well.

[b]Everything will be new and never seen before[/b], nothing from what you tried on ITCH will be included in the Alpha Demo. If the 2023 Concept Demo was a standalone echo of our potential, the August one will be GLASSHOUSE's definitive form. An important milestone that marks a turning point and a glimpse into the near future.
 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/2681373056dce1e3fe206994fbbfe0e4967bb4c0.png"][/img]
In [b]GLASSHOUSE - ALPHA DEMO[/b] you'll be able to test the following [b]content[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]ACT I - Chapter 1 fully playable (30+ minutes)[/p][/*][*][p]Combat System implemented[/p][/*][*][p]Political Compass redesigned[/p][/*][*][p]8 NPCs to meet, love and hate[/p][/*][*][p]Dormitory 73B freely explorable[/p][/*][*][p]Journal redesigned[/p][/*][*][p]Glossary implemented[/p][/*][*][p]New QTEs and PUZZLES in the Interaction Tab[/p][/*][*][p]UI/UX completely redesigned from scratch[/p][/*][*][p]Graphics improved and significantly optimized[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/f8075cacc81bde7e2b28df0235bf25504452ab8f.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]WHERE TO FIND US AT GAMESCOM[/h2][p]You'll find us at the INDIE AREA HALL, specifically in the [b]INDIE ARENA BOOTH[/b], among roughly 193 playable games. [b]GLASSHOUSE was selected from thousands of applications[/b] and for us it's truly a great honor to have our own booth, in what's recognized as the largest Indie Showcase ever. You'll find us there, beer in hand.

No seriously, come give us a hug, let's organize a dinner and maybe get lost together in the vast cosmos of informality. GLASSHOUSE is ours as much as it's yours.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/a85c9faa6db2088c9959272c7aa72d679320e0af.png"][/img][/p][h2]STEAM RELEASE[/h2][p][b]GLASSHOUSE - ALPHA DEMO[/b], shortly after Gamescom, will be released as a timed exclusive on our [url="https://discord.gg/HjPTxkfbCw" style="button"]Community Discord[/url], in the form of a Playtest, and [b]subsequently on Steam[/b]. We're almost there, we just want to make sure everything is perfect for the general public.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/0408911a962a28dbb344fe6f07ca07ff6455b8f5.png"][/img][/p][p]That's all for today and in the coming weeks, as we get closer to Gamescom, you can expect on these pages a series of [b]detailed updates on the Demo's content[/b]. It will be a great year for us and with this news-- it's just the beginning.
[i]
See you soon flatmates.

Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director FLAT28 Collective[/i][/p]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #10] Video Tour and Demo coming soon
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

Let's start with an important announcement: [b]this year we'll release the first Demo of Glasshouse on Steam[/b]. Due to circumstances beyond our control, we can't reveal the date yet -- just know that we've almost completed work on ACT I and this demo will be taken directly from a portion of it.

Now comes the most exciting part of development; [b]we're implementing dialogues, assets, and mechanics[/b], and what once seemed like an impossible puzzle to complete is now a wonderful interactive canvas. We want to celebrate GLASSHOUSE's [b]3rd birthday[/b] with a [b]video tour of Dormitory 73B[/b], one of the main settings, now finally connected between almost all its parts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/d1e1b6b5ab46e4cb099e76d84f4b27b1eb1ed25c.gif[/img]

[h2]SHARED SPACES: FROM GROUND FLOOR TO 3RD FLOOR[/h2]
Dormitory 73B consists of [b]four floors and six apartments[/b]; its past as an industrial slaughterhouse has allowed us to build an intricate and unpredictable level design, architecturally 'uncomfortable' and full of [b]secrets to discover[/b]. Each apartment is [b]completely explorable[/b] and directly mirrors the popular culture of the Lundonstoch fiefdom.

[previewyoutube=NYl34ZgMIE4;full][/previewyoutube]
While waiting to reveal more information about the Demo's release date, in the coming months we'll begin to show you in detail all the pillars that make up the definitive GLASSHOUSE experience, from the [b]Combat System[/b] to the [b]Political Compass[/b], including a [b]complete overhaul of the UI[/b] itself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/8f01e4c5d1e49e36aa367ee60c585f3b09903d20.gif[/img]

Since the release of the Concept Demo in 2023, we've been working tirelessly for over two years to reach this point -- 2025 is the year when Glasshouse will show itself in its definitive form: [b]new trailer[/b], public demo, press releases, [b]rebranding[/b] (new logo coming!), [b]a series of YouTube Devlogs[/b] and much more awaits you in this new phase of collective development.

In case you're wondering, no, [b]we still haven't found funding[/b] and work continues in our free time as it did in 2022. But as was the case three years ago, the flame that fuels our passion remains strong and with or without a publisher, [b]we will see this through to the end[/b]. That's a promise.

Thank you all, see you next month!

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #9] Visual Upgrades
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

I'm Andrea Marinelli, [b]Lead Technical Artist[/b] at [b]FLAT28[/b], and I am temporarily ousting Giacomo to create my first devblog. A techno-junkie one.

Over the past few months, [b]we’ve been focusing heavily on improving the visual side of Glasshouse[/b]. Our goal has been twofold: to define a clear visual identity and to set a benchmark for visual quality—a standard we aim to hit with every environment in the game.

To achieve that, we’ve been moving forward on multiple fronts. On one side, we kept working on new assets and building out the Dormitory 73B scenarios to maintain production momentum. On the other, we explored [b]new pipelines[/b] to speed up development while increasing overall visual fidelity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/83d83d06a493328c7ba9f7498d71942dd224b69d.gif[/img]

[h1]CLEANER EDGES & ROOM BORDERS[/h1]
We’ve [b]reworked the borders of every room[/b] and apartment in Dormitory 73B. The goal was to get a softer, [b]more natural separation between the interior and exterior parts[/b] of the rooms, while staying consistent with the aesthetic we're aiming for. The result feels more polished, cohesive, and true to our vision.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/5635922b37ff8dfef08443c5bf541d9268c547c3.gif[/img]

[h1]NEW POST-PROCESSING & OUTLINES[/h1]
One of the changes we're most excited about—and one you’ll likely notice right away—is a new post-processing effect that adds [b]subtle outlines across the entire scene[/b]. (well, might be actually tricky to get it via gif)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/8a7b1b0ab7df3bf241f5757bfd74bc807c44c4e8.gif[/img]

After testing various styles, we landed on an [b]outline shader that felt just right for the tone[/b] and identity of Glasshouse. Both the characters and environments now have a light contour that enhances detail and brings out the uniqueness of our art direction.

From an isometric top-down view, this effect also makes small details more readable, giving players a [b]clearer and sharper sense of space and depth[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7574251189c05e645cd3c7fa583ef1118b82d4c1.gif[/img]

[h1]CLOTH SIMULATION[/h1]
Until now, most of the cloth elements—curtains, drapes, and similar—were entirely static. That’s changing. We’ve begun integrating [b]real-time cloth simulation[/b] for selected elements.

Not all fabrics in the game will be dynamic, due to both performance considerations and artistic direction. But certain curtains and fabrics will now react to player interaction—swaying, shifting, or sliding over characters as they move through them. It’s a [b]small touch, but it adds a sense of life[/b] and responsiveness to the environments.

[h1]DLSS & UPSCALING EXPERIMENTS[/h1]

While it’s still early to talk in-depth about optimization, we’ve started preparing for it. [b]Glasshouse already supports NVIDIA DLSS 3[/b] internally, and we’re exploring dynamic resolution scaling and other upscaling techniques to ensure smooth performance across a wide range of hardware.

That’s all for now—but more is coming. We can’t wait to show you what’s next.

[i]Andrea Marinelli, Lead Technical Artist
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #8] Designing the perfect lockdown-story setting
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,  

today we bring you an update on the [b]progress of the main setting[/b] of Glasshouse, Dormitory 73B — and perhaps also a small reflection on the [b]architectural philosophy[/b] behind it.  

The compromise of privacy, inside and outside the lockdown.  

There isn’t a single member of FLAT28 who hasn’t lived outside of a condominium complex. Our entire lives, up until now, have always revolved around waiting for a crowded elevator that would never arrive, and that’s exactly where we started: [b]war in private spaces, coexistence in shared spaces[/b].  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/155e251d70344365e3bc008a6b2690809a1f9991.jpg[/img]  

[h2]GROUND FLOOR [GF][/h2]  
After a long day of work, you enter the lobby, and the number of [b]piled-up trash[/b] is only surpassed by the chaotic [b]tangle of notes plastered on the walls[/b]. "This place is not a dump / Taps will stop running water from 08:00 to 18:00 / The elevator is broken, call the technician."  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/c441f4907e2522fb45e5900be2a9c6d3f5136fc5.png[/img]  

The [b]Dormitory 73B[/b] is the perfect embodiment of this scenario, amplified beyond measure by the [b]lockdown[/b] conditions that the residents of the Lundonstoch fiefdom have endured for over 57 days. At first glance, the ground floor of this condominium is cold and unwelcoming. The pale color of the [b]concrete[/b] is almost blinding, and the [b]dense network of pipes[/b] weaves its way into private properties, forming a noose around the necks of those who live there.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/a008ad634c28b22d6a0cb8de9fd7db5b2605a864.png[/img]  

During the early 1900s, the [b]Grand Council of Lundonstoch[/b] promoted a collectivization effort aimed at [b]redeveloping old private factories into condominium complexes[/b]. Here, the industrial violently clashes with the residential — as if to remind us that we are all cogs in the great machine.  

There are no windows; they are not functional.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/3f8906bf19b6fd16080b9eff3b304712cb4176e5.jpg[/img]  

[h2]SECOND FLOOR [2F][/h2]  
Each [b]landing[/b] hosts two apartments, typically two-room units. The walls prefer to extend in height rather than width. The warm morning light filtering through the glass panels has turned this floor into a [b]small living room[/b] where neighbors gather for tea before heading to work.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/28525a716a2ce116c696b0de06b40eb4ba0a53dd.gif[/img]  

The goal was to banish the gray specter of the factory with furniture, rugs, and quilts. Although the management of shared spaces fell to the head-tenants, it had become common practice. In the Lundonstoch fiefdom, [b]every dormitory was a micro-society within society itself[/b].  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/edafdb48d68b7a8a9629f7307095b6b824976ebc.png[/img]  

The rules were established by the [b]head-tenant[/b] in charge through the [b]"Condominium Constitution"[/b] and could only be challenged by the arm of the fiefdom, the vassals of the Damage Control Brigade ([b]DCB[/b]), the authority.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/d16a5f07cb07aac6ed26d70b236e575f0e6c73d1.png[/img]  

[h2]TECHNOLOGY[/h2]  
For over 300 years, Lundonstoch relied on [b]Peat Power Plants[/b], an organic material formed from the partial decomposition of vegetation in waterlogged, acidic environments like marshes and moors.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/fcff1e340b79770a08b8d9096bd456e78845629c.png[/img]  

When a study in the 1980s revealed that the average life expectancy had dropped to 65 years and that infertility had reached 70% of the population, the Grand Feudal Council decided to implement a new, more efficient and less harmful system: [b]coal[/b].  

With the support of Devs from the fiefdom of [b]Ørstedia[/b], [b]Gravity Furnaces[/b] were quickly designed and distributed to all dormitories, leading to the temporary closure of all underground energy networks (Old Lundonstoch Canals) due to obsolescence.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/ca632db5732933a998c8679a49f7c974043de747.png[/img]  

This [b]energy decentralization[/b] operation effectively gave each dormitory a cumbersome heart, a maintenance room accessible only to the fiefdom’s technical operators. No tenant had access to it, not even the head-tenant.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/f622ee2c91f9389113b2546631fe1edd0f5cb0e6.jpg[/img]  

The one adapted in Glasshouse, as you can see, is an [b]inductive Narrative Design[/b] that starts from the micro to better understand the macro. Private property is nothing more than a small window into the vast society of [b]The World of Glass[/b].  

We are a small team, [b]we couldn’t afford to create an open world[/b], so we rolled up our sleeves and drew from what we know best: thin air, crumbling corridors, and small rooms/spaces overflowing with stories. When [b]COVID-19[/b] forced us into our condominiums for months, it wasn’t a huge tragedy — we already had everything we needed, our [b]small self-governed ecosystem[/b].  

Thank you all, see you next month!  

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director  
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #7] Screenplay and Arcweave implementation
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

today the sky in Milan is clear, suspended in a greyish haze that timidly envelops our colorful souls. David Lynch has passed away, and I'm sitting in front of my creaky desk, in a 57-square-meter apartment, trying to conceptualize the words of the [b]first Glasshouse update of 2025[/b]. It’s a good day to write.

Today we talk about the [b]progress made on the Glasshouse script[/b], narrative methodologies, and artistic innocence.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/e2dad4b3dd38a74e45a290b7dd9ecf3a558a2717.png[/img]

[b]PROLOGUE & ACT 1[/b]

87 pages, 24,831 black words printed on a pale 27-inch screen. Last December, both the [b]Prologue and Act 1 of Glasshouse were officially completed[/b] and revised. Glasshouse’s script is extremely complex, a chimera whose shape is even elusive to us.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/42ad8fa5e00dbe6a17d29b5224ca40d370bc79a9.png[/img]

[b]In 2021, the World of Glass was only the concept of a blog[/b] consisting of front pages of newspapers from all the feudal republics of the world. The idea was to tell the disintegration of the foundations of civil society under the shadow of a war-torn storm.

If [b]Hobbes[/b] spoke of the state as a [b]Leviathan[/b] necessary to prevent chaos through the centralization of powers, with [b]Glasshouse[/b], I wanted to propose a [b]short circuit[/b], a reflection on the possible return to decentralization, but this time with a civilization and a people strengthened by the lessons learned during the era of globalization. What would happen to our society if liberalism were excluded for over 200 years from the equation of a capitalist economic system?

If it weren’t for Authoritarian or Oligarchic Capitalism, [b]what could a new alternative be, perhaps decentralized and ultra-democratic[/b]?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/4a7d871d5b9dec10620fc6452842060a8a852451.png[/img]

When the World of Glass became Glasshouse in 2022, the wars of our planet forced us to think about the geopolitical and social setup of tomorrow. [b]Today the situation is more fragile than yesterday[/b], the questions have multiplied like mushrooms, and [b]Glasshouse, on the other hand, needs to feed on contemporaneity[/b] to offer a reflection in line with the times.

The plausibility of a new world requires time, love, and constant doubt. Finally, after complete rewrites and violent proofreading, we made it. [b]When I started to suffer for the characters I killed, that’s when I realized it was all real[/b], and that I had to and could finally move forward.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/87e93eff0429915c8c08f4a6ab832e2df08574a1.png[/img]

[b]IMPLEMENTATION OF ARCWEAVE[/b]

In 2023, following the departure of our former Lead Programmer and the arrival of the current one, Samuele, we made the decision to [b]completely rewrite the dialogue management system[/b].

After carefully exploring Twine and Articy Draft, in the end, [b]we decided to form a partnership with Arcweave[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/919f5bdaf15f01f34dcc6e36a20f19377fc386bc.jpg[/img]

With the introduction of Arcweave, we took the time to [b]completely restart from scratch[/b]. If dialogues were previously managed entirely through code, now implementation happens through a [b]node-based practical system[/b].

Through [b]Play Mode[/b], we can also preview the newly added dialogues as if they were a sort of [b]graphic novel[/b]. It may seem like a small feature, but it greatly helps us understand the effectiveness of narrative beats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/ddb38cb15246cb2b9384cca7f6133dfe3710a6f8.gif[/img]

Arcweave’s introduction was certainly a productive move that slowed us down, but we are sure it’s also [b]a crucial investment that will save us time in the future[/b], both for proofreading and for the fast implementation of dialogues and localizations through APIs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/9e3be9d732643ebca7b21828fa6cca7e151743e8.png[/img]

[b]BEATCHART AND WIREFRAME[/b]

The method used to outline the events of Glasshouse is called [b]Save The Cat[/b] and was developed by [b]Blake Snyder[/b]. For those unfamiliar, this method, unlike the classic board with post-its forming the three acts, offers [b]a rigid 15 "beat" narrative structure[/b] that deconstructs the act structure itself and helps build a well-balanced one.

The 15 beats are as follows:
[b]1)[/b] Opening Image  
[b]2)[/b] Theme Stated  
[b]3)[/b] Setup  
[b]4)[/b] Catalyst  
[b]5)[/b] Debate  
[b]6)[/b] Break Into Act Two  
[b]7)[/b] B Story  
[b]8)[/b] Fun and Games  
[b]9)[/b] Midpoint  
[b]10)[/b] Bad Guys Close In  
[b]11)[/b] All Is Lost  
[b]12)[/b] Dark Night of the Soul  
[b]13)[/b] Break Into Act Three  
[b]14)[/b] Finale  
[b]15)[/b] Final Image

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/29e32f3dcc36da07379fe5d093d3c6943b810fe2.png[/img]

Once we had the 15 beats of Glasshouse, the derived High Concept allowed me to organize a [b]Wireframe[/b] that expanded these beats into a dense web of events/quests.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/9ce79960cdd5c5d75e6809be762261dd6e58cce0.png[/img]

As mentioned in several places, I am not a video game writer, I am a filmmaker, and adapting this writing system to a video game context has been a great challenge. It’s a bet that took a lot of time, and only now is it starting to show the benefits of the effort.

When Glasshouse is in your hands, [b]we hope you will appreciate our experiments[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/4292544a7550c50d9bd7ddcdfc062a4f29432040.png[/img]

The sky of Milan is still suspended between light and darkness, and the windows of the concrete monoliths are beginning to emit heat. [b]That’s all for today[/b], I hope you found this [b]Behind The Writing[/b] interesting.

Thanks to all of you, but especially thanks to you, Lynch. All in all, it’s been a good day.  
See you soon!

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director  
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: GLASSHOUSE - FAQ #1
notes.content:
Hello flatmates!

In light of recent updates, many questions have arisen about Glasshouse and its future, so we want to take the opportunity to put together a handy FAQ and [b]get ready for 2025[/b], a year that will hold [b]many surprises[/b].

[h1]So, let's get into it![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/3f2958fd6db8b3057e89946da2730d08d2ad32e0.gif[/img]

[u]Q: What is Glasshouse?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Glasshouse is an isometric Turn-Based-CRPG set in a post-capitalist feudalpunk world at the dawn of a terrible world war. Inspired by RPGs such as Disco Elysium and Pathologic, Glasshouse promises an intense narrative-roleplaying experience punctuated by unforgettable characters, complex dialogue trees, multiple endings and deep ideological introspections that go beyond the screen.

[u]Q: What's the Plot of Glasshouse?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] The entire fiefdom is in lockdown when a mysterious triple murder occurs in your apartment building. Unknowingly, you are caught up in a political conspiracy bigger than yourself. Find a way out or find yourself.

[u]Q: Who is the developer FLAT28?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] We are an international art collective consisting of 17 members from the film, CGI and video game industries. We have been working on Glasshouse since 2022 in our spare time, without salaries, funding or publishers. Completely smart working.

[u]Q: What's Feudalpunk?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Feudalpunk is a fictional subgenre that mixes elements of the feudal era with contemporary themes or technologies, focusing on social themes such as class struggle and the sharp contrast between them. In Glasshouse's post-capitalist world, following the revolution of 1828, the geopolitical order has overthrown the state model in favour of the democratic feudal model. Inspired by the Kurdish manifesto of Democratic Confederalism, Glasshouse imagines a deglobalised world where technological progress has come to a standstill and the economic-social gap between fiefdoms is unbridgeable, where 100km distance between one fiefdom and another can be equivalent to 100 years of technological difference.

[u]Q: Does Glasshouse have a combat system?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Yes, as announced a few months ago, Glasshouse will have turn-based combat inspired by older Final Fantasy and the more recent Fear & Hunger.

[u]Q: When is the Release Date?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Too early to announce it.

[u]Q: Are you planning an Early Access Release?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] No, no early access release is currently planned.

[u]Q: Are you planning a Kickstarter campaign?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] It depends on many factors, first and foremost, the general interest around Glasshouse in these early stages. Kickstarter has changed over time and a proper campaign may require a lot of funding, which we currently do not have.

[u]Q: Will there be voice acting?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] The aim is to have Glasshouse, for the launch, at least with partial voice acting. To date, as there is no publisher, it is difficult to say for sure.

[u]Q: How long will Glasshouse be?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] We expect to have a main campaign between 10 and 15 hours. We are a small team (without budget) and want to create a strong, intense and highly replayable experience. For our ambitions, it is necessary to reduce the duration to have an rpg component that really makes a difference. 

[u]Q: Are there any DLC planned?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] We have at least one expansion of the main story in mind, but nothing is certain. It will depend a lot on how the development of Glasshouse proceeds and on sales. Let's be clear, we are not talking about cut content, but a possible small additional story that will give another point of view to the main plot.

[u]Q: What is the Concept Demo of Glasshouse?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] A small 3-hour standalone experience from the first 2022 builds of Glasshouse, when we were young and didn't yet know what we were doing. It is a vertical slice mainly designed to sell the settings, atmospheres and core game mechanics to publishers. Nothing included in the concept demo will be present in the final Glasshouse game. You can download it from [url=https://flat28-collective.itch.io/glasshouseconcept]Itch.io[/url].

[u]Q: Why was the Concept Demo removed from Steam?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] It was originally conceived in 2022 for pitching to Publishers, and later adapted to a wider audience to gather feedback, experiment and fine-tune our production pipeline. Now, two years later, this version no longer represents the final product and for this reason, we have decided to remove it.

[u]Q: Will the game be available on GOG and other stores?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] It’ll likely be available on GOG and EPIC Store.

[u]Q: Will preorders be available?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] No. ♥♥♥♥ preorders.

[u]Q: What platforms other than PC are planned for release?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] We’re planning releases for PS5 and Xbox S/X, likely following the PC release.

[u]Q: What engine is the game being developed in?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Unity.

[u]Q: How can I get in touch with the devs?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] You can write us at prj.glasshouse@gmail.com or join our [url=https://discord.gg/HjPTxkfbCw] Discord [/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7493d54596c091c2cb1ffb076071f102d3eddaed.gif[/img]

That's it for this year, and I want to take this space to make a promise: [b]from 2025 onwards you can expect a devblog every month[/b], with the aim of offering an ever-expanding window on the stormy development journey of the FLAT28 collective. Making video games isn't easy, but damn if it's fun.

We can't wait to reveal [b]the future of Glasshouse[/b] to you.

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #6] Building the combat system of Glasshouse
notes.content:
Hello compeers,

welcome back to our little [b]Autonomous Social Center[/b], where we generally take ourselves a bit more seriously and shed some light on that chimera known as Glasshouse. In recent months, the collective has accelerated development thanks to a [b]paradigm shift in our production structure[/b]. With pre-production now completed, I've officially[b] handed over the reins of project management to Gianmarco[/b], [b]leaving me more time to focus on the script and the artistic/creative direction[/b] of it. Gianmarco, who has been a Game Designer on Glasshouse since 2022 and has gained valuable experience managing Handmancers (a parallel project developed by 58Blades), proposed that the collective adopt the [b]"Agile methodology"[/b]: In essence, we have replaced Trello with Notion, embracing a more systemic approach to development based on [b]flexible sprints[/b], instead of rigid deadlines. We have also increased the number of weekly meetings, and now [b]each department is fully autonomous[/b], which is a result of past decisions to create windows, not walls, toward each other's work. If[b] Glasshouse is a collective stream of consciousness[/b], then FLAT28 is a social funnel channeling it.

Today, for the first time, we will show you the Combat System prototype, but we will also take a look at the Sidescroll sections and the new residents who will join soon Dorm 73B.

[previewyoutube=qmHlLC4avzc;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]EARLY COMBAT SYSTEM PROTOTYPE[/b]

Against all production-commercial logic, the combat system in Glasshouse is [b]designed to be in ludonarrative harmony[/b]. The goal is to create [b]non-repetitive combat[/b] instances that exist only when they make narrative sense. If we think of the pacing of the game like an electrocardiogram, we want Glasshouse's combat to be a fleeting peak, not a flatline between narrative beats. For this reason, we decided that there will only be [b]six combat encounters[/b] in total, two of which are entirely optional.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/a057a4d201d5532ff8748c6888d069099ec4cc92.png[/img]

The combat system in Glasshouse is inspired by the classic turn-based combat of [b]Final Fantasy[/b], with a touch of puzzle-game logic à la [b]Fear & Hunger[/b]. Each turn, you can choose to attack the enemy, talk to them, or change your equipment. If [b]"Attack"[/b] involves a dice roll (which varies based on the equipped weapon) that damages the enemy's [b]health bar[/b], [b]"Talk"[/b] offers a path of negotiation through dialogue lines that scale based on your [b]Political Compass[/b]. Just like you, the enemy also has their own Political Compass, and if you manage to "strike the right chord," you can severely damage their [b]Threat Bar[/b]. This is a holistic value that determines the degree of influence you can exert on the opponent: if your Threat Bar is higher than the enemy's, you can attempt to make them surrender. Changing equipment, on the other hand, allows you to sacrifice a turn to select different weapons (which influence Wealdmaer's Threat Bar), heal, or even alter the outcome of the battle in unexpected ways.

What you're seeing here is an [b]early in-development prototype[/b] and does not represent the final stage of this mechanic, especially in terms of UI, SFX, and VFX, where we've relied primarily on functional [b]placeholders[/b].

[previewyoutube=QdYRXZbB9vs;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]SIDESCROLL SEQUENCES[/b]

As we mentioned in the last Devblog, we've been working for months on the new sidescroll sections that will make their debut in Glasshouse. While remaining [b]a primarily isometric cRPG[/b], we've decided to introduce sidescrolling sequences (where you can still move in three dimensions) in cramped rooms and decaying corridors with the aim of [b]changing perspectives in level and quest design[/b], favoring a more varied and stimulating exploration pace. Additionally, for us, it's also a way to immerse you even further into the claustrophobic environments of Glasshouse, and maybe even hide some easter eggs for the sharp-eyed players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/6d0f7aa18ed9c30a4c2c6b035026024d8e71d35e.png[/img]

[b]THE GIRL FROM DORM 72[/b]

Victim of events or architect of circumstances?
[b]Lia[/b] is officially ready to enter the [b]modeling phase[/b], and above you can see the turn-around concept.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/f670f0cf1e833b060c093ef7fd18b2d873bbfe18.png[/img]

[b]THE DORM LEADER[/b]

Valerio, our 3D Character Artist, shows us the [b]completed texturing of Makenna[/b]. Soon, she will be rigged by Federico and will be ready to exercise her democracy in Dorm 73B.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/623f94440f4d4980a091a55319a1ab90e325f076.png[/img]

Today's devblog was an experiment: showing you early development material (like the Combat System) allows us to [b]gather feedback that, at this stage, can truly make a difference[/b]. Help us shape the Glasshouse you want to play, especially now that [b]we don't have a publisher and can do what we want[/b].

Thanks everyone, see you soon compeers!

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #5] New Features, Characters and Environments
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

Glasshouse has officially been in [b]Full-Production for about 4 months now[/b] and today we're going to show you some of the new stuff we've been working on, including [b]unique camera features[/b] and [b]environments[/b] beyond Dormitory 73B.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/6855994b95069f1de8363f5edad8556ea95b4a2f.gif[/img]

[b]SIDE-SCROLLING SEQUENCES[/b]

GLASSHOUSE will feature [b]game sections in which the camera abandons isometry[/b] in favour of a closer, more intimate perspective. This choice was mainly dictated by the desire to include narrow spaces to [b]amplify the suffocating feeling of lockdown[/b]. Generally, [b]narrow rooms and isometric views entail sacrifices in terms of artistry and navigability[/b], so it was a natural process for us to opt for this camera switch. To be clearer, about[b] 10% of Glasshouse will feature side-scrolling sections[/b]. Don't worry, we love the isometric perspective, we are not abandoning it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/a014e31671db8490e9aaf4642743956fb11fc033.png[/img]

Speaking of exploration, [b]this new perspective allows us to hide clues and interactions[/b] in a completely different way than before. This camera experimentation, on the other hand, is nothing more than the [b]expansion of the philosophy behind Cineshots[/b], with which we already portrayed specific pivotal moments of dialogue in the Concept Demo.

We are confident that these sections will be[b] a great tool to offer variety[/b], both in terms of narrative and gameplay. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7490c5d57a6bfedc2147f1f182ee5423ffc394c6.png[/img]

[b]NEW CHARACTERS[/b]

We have[b] three new tenants[/b] to introduce to you: Makenna, Hildebrand and Lia!
[b]Makenna[/b], flat 24, is almost a [b]mother figure[/b] for our protagonist. When Godwyne died of Pitch Black, in fact, Makenna took care of her son Wealdmaer, as a promise of friendship.

Makenna is currently being modelled and you can see the progress being made below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/dcf57df13247a519c085e5288f61d1a18b4a636f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/90b540679902c44839e7ffacd37dae1c7bb3d882.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/ff72fd36f088a4dda4575a8aa58224a201c740b4.png[/img]

[b]Hildebrand[/b], flat 29, is a retired DCB veteran. He suffers from dementia, hates foreigners and [b]believes he is still in service[/b], as evidenced by his battered uniform.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/811b3250d36d69925df9390d3cf68379011aea1d.jpg[/img]

[b]Lia[/b] is a colleague from Factory No. 3, her residence is in another dormitory though, the 74A. [b]Her presence in 73B is not welcome[/b]. Below is a first draft (not final).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/067c090814ebe68d14572dfd2584fd196cf3ac0a.png[/img]

[b]BEYOND THE DORMITORY[/b]

Through the Old Canals of Lundonstoch, it will be possible to reach [b]the surface of Wynstann's Quarter 73[/b] and open the doors of the [b]Weird Wires, the Abandoned Theatre[/b]. After countless changes of management, the contract for the Weird Wires was [b]illegally taken away by the Percival Consortium[/b], a criminal organisation suspected to be at the helm of the CoFoPo terrorist union.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/f8710b741f05d9f1afe7fe4015fc564fd4d44245.png[/img]

For Wealdmaer, the Weird Wires is [b]a temple of memories[/b], a stage where one can be anyone, anywhere. Even now, in the night, Wealdmaer will wander the glorious corridors of that possible future, together with his late father Godwyne.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/39d986fd42063d666cd1a9d0c0881d5e3e7a61dd.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7e3c53c68daa2e73f04ca516ac61f68d95f506f8.png[/img]

From the Fiefdom of Lundonstoch it's all, the [b]FLAT28[/b] Collective is back at work.
Thank you all, see you soon!

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: GLASSHOUSE: Concept Demo now available!
notes.content:
Hello Compeers,

[b]Glasshouse's Concept Demo is officially available on Steam[/b] and today we want to celebrate this moment with you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/bfe20cc28213a83339b3189d2cc483a2a312911e.png[/img]

[b][h2]FLAT28, A COLLECTIVE WITHOUT HOPE[/h2][/b]
Italy, Bulgaria, England, USA, Canada, Austria, Colombia.
[b]The FLAT28 Collective was born with impossible assumptions[/b]: Connecting human beings from distant continents to develop one or more video games, in an increasingly dark and detached world.
When the embryo of GLASSHOUSE first came into existence, [b]never, ever did we expect to find ourselves here[/b], 2 years later, in front of the "Release Build" button.

By May 2022, GLASSHOUSE was just a pile of gray blocks, dozens of word pages, and some timid artwork, amid literary, video game, and movie inspirations.

[b]Today, we officially close the chapter of "Pre-Production"[/b] and embark on the stormy sea of GLASSHOUSE's actual development.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/38cec80524f7edb91967fbe56a6ecba8e351fab6.png[/img]

[b][h2]THE MEANING OF "CONCEPT DEMO"[/h2][/b]
[b]This Concept Demo does not represent the final product[/b] and probably does not even do it full justice. [b]This is the Videoludic Manifesto of a dozen artists[/b] (professional and non-professional), developed in our spare time, without funding, over nearly 700 days.

We were naive, we fought and finally loved.
That's part of the game of independent development, you destroy to create, you change to improve.

This Concept Demo does not represent the final product simply because, over time, we have changed. We write better than yesterday, we model better than yesterday, we plan better than the day before yesterday.

Most likely, the contents of this experience will be entirely cut, torn, and stitched back together in different guises once the final form of GLASSHOUSE is on display sooner or later. Take this Demo as[b] a kind of "Chapter that will be lost in time."[/b]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #4] Cops Don't Bark, new demo coming soon!
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

After 5 months of silence, we are back with good news: [b]GLASSHOUSE pre-production is officially over![/b]

Take a big breath, in the next few lines of this DevBlog we will dwell on the [b]new Demo[/b] and what is involved in leaving the pre-production phase for the [b]FLAT28 Collective[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/b3c5b95b72e68fa9ee3ba2b2f812baae5cd4eb13.png[/img]

[b]COPS DON'T BARK, THE NEW DEMO[/b].

Over the past year we've been working hard to create [b]the best possible concept[/b] of GLASSHOUSE, a virtual gym within which to develop mechanics and systems, the foundation of our video game. If [b]LivingRoom_Build[/b] (The demo currently playable on our [url=https://discord.gg/w597G3BVJM]Discord[/url]) represented the more dialogic soul of GLASSHOUSE, [b]Cops Don't Bark introduces the exploratory element[/b], implements high-requested features, and amplifies the depth of quest design.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/8cfaf1c57dc8dbb0698e9f41b17c3ffd424765e6.png[/img]

First of all, Cops Don't Bark will introduce[b] two new settings[/b], Canal 73 and Wealdmaer's Room. The [b]Canal 73[/b] opens the door to the underground network of the [b]Old Canals of Lundonstoch[/b], a dark labyrinth manned by patrols of the Control Damage Brigade. 

The Old Canals represent an opportunity for us to create a [b]more complex level design[/b] than the canonical geometries of Dormitory 73B, so expect [b]hidden passages[/b], [b]environmental puzzles[/b] and a more extensive pacing!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/209a6825664abdc5da180e4b258f7c56d61c1140.png[/img]

[b]Wealdmaer's room[/b], as mentioned in the previous DevBlog, is part of the natural evolution process of apartment 28, the central HUB of GLASSHOUSE. Within it,[b] the player will be able to craft tools, equipment[/b] (did anyone ask for "more Inventory slots"?), deposit resources and[b] thoroughly investigate the past of their avatar[/b]. After all, we are intruders in the head of the protagonist, who wants to deny us information vital to our survival. We have opted for a bottom-up characterization approach, Wealdmaer's room in fact is a temple of memories waiting to be discovered on multiple levels. Of all, the idea that [b]each player may have a different degree of knowledge of Wealdmaer[/b] is one of the elements that excites us most.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/b096acb5bcacfe4c4aa00a0a33be54431f64ffd2.png[/img]

[b]JOURNAL, QUALITY OF LIFE AND CONTROLLER SUPPORT[/b].

By pressing the "J" key, it is now possible to consult [b]Wealdmaer's Personal Journal[/b], within which it will be possible to [b]keep track of progress[/b] and get useful advice on carrying out quests. Don't call it a quest-log, because it's so much more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/9062a3eb0f88a7a34bf7deeee6ac2b5f743b3c18.png[/img]

We are also happy to report the [b]full compatibility of GLASSHOUSE with controllers and WASD [/b]support for movement. But it doesn't end here, these days Andrea and Gianmarco are working hard on the implementation of a much requested feature during the previous playtests, the [b]overline of interactive objects[/b]! This feature will allow the player to more easily locate interacting objects during mouse exploration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/23fb5c27323311264a123d7181d263d55691e1f8.png[/img]

[b]NEW 3D MODELS[/b].

GLASSHOUSE can now enjoy[b]new 3D models for its characters[/b], who now show up in [b]significantly more detailed guises[/b] and with a consistent artstyle vis-à-vis the new portraits. This increase in quality was a not inconsiderable investment of time, but it now allows us to take much closer shots than before, going on to [b]greatly expand the directing possibilities[/b] during dialogues!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7da53ff8b954cbd2f373a9446c5e6a635b4558be.png[/img]

[b]GLASSHOUSE ENTERS PRODUCTION[/b].

With the introduction of the [b]Political Compass[/b] (which we will discuss in detail in the next DevBlog) in Cops Don't Bark, [b]GLASSHOUSE is officially "Feature complete"[/b] and we are ready to move out of the pre-production phase. This means that [b]we have all the systems we need to develop GLASSHOUSE, from start to finish[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/9d078f1260c9e6ac868b492605a2c5690a4c1091.png[/img]

As anticipated in the July DevBlog, GLASSHOUSE underwent a major [b]redesign[/b] over the two years of development: [b]In the absence of publishers or investors[/b], reducing the content scope was a necessary choice to focus the development of a game that was born with too much ambition. We are human beings, and like all developers struggling with their first game, we made miscalculations out of inexperience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/301e9a53e550c0702677f2a0496c360a9c320af9.png[/img]

However, as it was born, [b]we still decided to continue the development of GLASSHOUSE in our spare time[/b], without funding. Cops Don't Bark is a concept and as such, it will mark the end of one journey and the beginning of a new one. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/0625b2c095576380a3f9a47213ee055d3c4f8ac7.png[/img]

[b]Cops Don't Bark will be released by December 2023[/b] on our [b]Discord[/b] and on [b]Itch.io[/b], after which, we will continue full steam ahead, treading the path of [b]self-publication[/b]. For us, telling the story of the flatmates of Apartment 28 is a necessity, and one way or another, we will succeed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/b72a9e8dd42be1e6e6ac1606002706a7b0d449df.jpg[/img]

We close this DevBlog with a letter dedicated to all those fighting their own war: [b]In November[/b], during Milan Games Week, [b]for the first time part of the collective met in person[/b]. One cannot describe the joy of putting a face to the people with whom one has been communicating uninterruptedly for about two years, behind a black screen. [b]This DevBlog is for all of us, for the collective, for those who have left and for those who remain[/b].


Thank you all.

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
Collettivo FLAT28[/i]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #3] Dungeon, new UI and much more!
notes.content:
Hello mates,

It has been four months since the last Dev-Blog and now it is finally time to tell you about [b]the challenges[/b] we have faced along this tortuous journey and what still lies ahead.

First, at present, the development of [b]GLASSHOUSE has not yet been funded and is proceeding by volunteerism, passion and ambition[/b]. Despite this, the [b]FLAT28[/b] collective is more determined and united than ever. In early 2023, with our feet on the ground and our hearts in our hands, [b]we decided to transform GLASSHOUSE into a less dilated and more intense/focused game[/b].

[b]We redesigned the narrative and design side[/b] in such a way as to scale back costs, ambitions, and development timelines. Looking in the mirror, being self-critical and making decisions is part of the game, a game we espouse with dedication and seriousness.

Initially envisioned as a story between the sunset of a society and an apocalyptic dawn, recent structural changes will lead GLASSHOUSE to focus on the sunset, which is the last day of a world torn apart by wars and borders. [b]The opportunity is huge and is to be able to focus on the emotional sphere of 18 residents of an apartment building frightened by the idea that there may be no tomorrow[/b]. It is the story of those who grit their teeth and struggle against the inexorable. It is the story of us all.

Now follow us below, the seeds we planted have finally borne fruit and we can't wait to show them to you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/ee6fe0f399fc9a916934b669480bc0ae5225b388.gif[/img]

[b]THE OLD CANALS[/b]

The Fiefdom of Lundonstoch is under lockdown due to atomic threat and no one is allowed to leave their homes on pain of imprisonment or death. However, in the course of the adventure, the housemates of Apartment 28 will be forced to embark on a dangerous journey that will see them traverse [b]the underground districts of the Wynnstan[/b] quarter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/f757e94299d0653bd98616ddc1ea1e223bc717be.png[/img]

The Old Canals of Wynnstan are the roots of the neighborhood, [b]a dreary maze of pipes and bricks[/b] within which death waits patiently. [b]A veritable dungeon studded with hidden treasures, mysteries and past history[/b]. In 1828, during the Rifle Strike, they were used by the New Youth as a hiding place from capitalist power. Today, the canals are [b]refuge for tramps and criminal syndicates[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/dbdef6f5cb78462d56c439ad2797f50be946028d.png[/img]

This new setting is located under Dormitory 73B, the main setting of GLASSHOUSE, and is [b]currently being greyboxed[/b]. The goal of our 3D Environment Dept. is to test a [b]new workflow based on asset modularity[/b], so that detailed and complex settings can be created more efficiently. Huge shout out to Simona, Andrea, Giuseppe, Marco and Camilo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/75e811d6190d42149af58744402e70550981c178.png[/img]

[b]THE PLAYER'S ROOM[/b]

We have recently completed Wealdmaer's room, located inside apartment 28, the private space where you can craft items, store resources, and watch the city change, out the window.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/c554ddfed0d6244a05ba58c73995191224a4b079.png[/img]

We have created this room for you and Wealdmaer, a safe place from lies and political pitfalls. We look forward to seeing you there, sitting before the window, pondering the inexorability of life and the futility of war.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/957de0dde76aef545a530f062a7601d4f76d3190.jpg[/img]

[b]NEW UI: PORTRAITS AND DIALOGUE TAB[/b]

Over the past months, the art department has been working hard on replacing the placeholder assets in the User Interface. Giancarlo, Character Designer, has created the [b]final character portraits[/b], now more in line with the three-dimensional models and Key-Art.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/b610bf9138fc1bf195f0354495367b772d0afc63.png[/img]

Nino and Umberto, UI Designer and Art Director respectively, recently delivered the [b]new dialog interface[/b]. After the playtest that took place in our Discord community, the goal was to make the design more appealing and improve text readability. As you can see, new icons and mechanics also find their way into the lower left space, but we will have to elaborate on this in the future!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/e77515beb804ef536e9753df4ee3f8487deab515.png[/img]

[b]THE JOURNAL[/b]

Our programmer Mav meanwhile shows us the first iterations of the Journal.
The player will have a way to [b]consult the Journal as a quest-log or keep track of past adventures[/b].
GLASSHOUSE is meant to be immersion first, and to avoid a simple to-do list, we decided to take inspiration from the Darkwood system. Little information, but good information.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/37ecc89d9535f675ead59fbeeceb581375b70c2f.jpg[/img]

[b]NEW 3D MODELS[/b]

Not satisfied with the level previously achieved, we opted for a [b]complete overhaul of the 3D models of the characters[/b]. Thanks to [url=https://www.artstation.com/valeriobarchi]Valerio[/url], Wealdmaer was completely redesigned from scratch so as to be as faithful as possible to the original concepts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/41d66fdff7c11acd2b44377ccb544c164bb70503.png[/img]

We still have much more to show you, but that is all for today. We hope you have enjoyed the news and the transparency with which we talk about our difficulties. The journey is still long, but brick by brick, we will make it if you are still with us.

Thank you all.

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Game Director
FLAT28 Collective[/i].

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #2] The Art of Glasshouse
notes.content:
Hello humans,

In this dev blog we'd like to tell you about the philosophy behind the making of one of our protagonists, [b]Dormitory73B[/b], the setting for [b]Glasshouse[/b]!

[b]FLAT28[/b] is a collective of about 20 people who, during our spare time, set out to tell [b]the story of a proletarian community in a new society[/b], a new world. Given the big elephant in the room (lack of any kind of budget), it was immediately clear that an open world formula would never work.

How to deal with the harsh reality accordingly?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/1f0a4e4f2d24aff7e583d3a07f9c5ab4357ce9fd.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Our approach has been to work in the small context. [b]Private property is an honest mirror of society[/b]. The furnishing of a flat or its architecture are not just goods, but can be a means of storytelling.
[/list]

Often in cRPGs interiors are just a point B between the journey from A to B, in Glasshouse the apartment building is all that is left of a society in the throes of a [b]nuclear revolution[/b].
Wealdmaer, the player, finds himself in a lockdown situation forced by events he cannot escape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/195b2b07cb9876e49a2a3628028478464710b232.png[/img]

[list]
[*] We therefore took inspiration from the giants creators of closed worlds such as [b]Resident Evil[/b] and Haunting Ground, gaming experiences that were able to build a [b]complex and intricate level design[/b] from a single building.
[/list]

Dormitory 73B is a privileged opportunity to get to know and touch the [b]private sphere of Lundonstoch Feud society[/b]. The apartment building will provide unprecedented stimuli for exploration, between [b]shared residential spaces[/b] and [b]private flats[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/f00751ab11d7d771ea3ad826c22bbb9659f02341.png[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Apartment 28 is the central hub[/b] of Glasshouse, the home of the protagonist and his housemates, Ecgberth and Voitsehk. Two floors in which to [b]interact with each small asset[/b] in order to obtain resources useful for survival or progress in the main story.
[/list]

In Glasshouse, the exploration of the containers does not stop at the simple "click > drag > drop" but presents a system in which [b]textual exploration[/b] can turn out to be a labyrinth of options that conceal unprecedented interactions. For instance, a seemingly innocuous bookcase could hide [b]secret compartments[/b] or the structure itself could be deprived of [b]components such as nails and wood[/b], useful for crafting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/672246ca1c30fa5ed0f1713bb3ab317f9d8837df.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] Like a Matryoshka doll, in fact, the architecture and furniture of Dormitory 73B can offer [b]different levels of interaction[/b] at various times during the main quest, whether it be [b]dialogue options unlocked by certain tools[/b] or codes for suitcases belonging abandoned by past housemates.
[/list]

Each polygonal model has a story to tell (literally, inanimate objects can talk to you and are in fact NPCs with personalities, but that's another story) and is a founding part of the world building of a post-capitalist society where privatisation is at historical limits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/bf94110713b5e9ae8737cdc20fc4e1f1bd20ad47.gif[/img]

That is why we also decided to make the [b]isometric view closer[/b], we want the player to be able to perceive time and space better. In Glasshouse, the camera can abandon the isometric view to immerse the player even more in the nooks and crannies of the apartment building. The [b]change of perspective[/b] as a game philosophy, both in form and content!


Thank you so much, that's all for today, see ya next time!

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Game Director
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #1] What is Glasshouse?
notes.content:
Hello humans,

If you have followed previous updates, you will know by now what the [b]FLAT28 collective[/b] is all about, and so it is time to open the dances of what will be a long series of updates to the multimedia experience that goes by the name of[b] GLASSHOUSE[/b]. Glasshouse is first and foremost a cRPG, one where you talk a lot and think actively about the past, present and future of the story you find yourself in.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/43329820/8567d3559a6ff33ade979e9f410f76663befc843.gif[/img]

We at FLAT28, however, have not stopped at paying homage to a genre that is very dear to us, and it is in fact from the need to remodel a game system that is currently undergoing a sort of renaissance that we have decided to graft survival elements to give life to what we call[b] Survival cRPG[/b].

The player, once his skill points have been assigned to the [b]political orientation system[/b], will take on the role of [b]Wealdmaer of Godwyne[/b], a humble labourer [b]stuck within the crumbling walls of a proletariat apartment block following the explosion of an atomic bomb[/b] within a few kilometres.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/43329820/ac0bab956f68499ff29b9d971e57200efb9c4af9.gif[/img]

In the shadow of an ongoing nuclear winter,[b] Dormitory 73B[/b] will turn into a social microcosm where class struggle will result in an upheaval of hierarchies and laws. If the world glimpsed through the windows is in flames, the apartment block is alive and pulsating, [b]a new reactionary societal order[/b]. When [b]Wealdmaer finds during his morning patrol the battered corpse of the head of the condo[/b], disturbing rumours about [b]CoFoPo Union spies[/b] inside the complex begin to circulate in the gloomy, poorly lit corridors of the dormitory.

As tensions inevitably rise, it will be up to Wealdmaer, elected deputy head of condominium, to prevent the witch hunt from turning into a [b]civil war between the floors of the complex[/b]. Player's choices will shape the epilogue of Glasshouse.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/43329820/bdf7fc9ade7eaf3abc2ee2ef7e4e3c979a5fb2a9.gif[/img]

I almost forgot, the world of Glasshouse is not the world you know and in fact you will be surprised to realise that although aesthetically the story may appear to be set in Victorian times, we are actually in 2028. March 2028 A.E. to be precise, two hundred years after what we call 'The Shattering' or[b] the age of decentralisation in which globalisation and the nation-state concept was cast aside in favour of a democratic world system based on Feud[/b].

In the future we will go into detail about the [b]World Building[/b] and various game systems such as Political Orientation, [b]Comfort System[/b], [b]Crafting[/b] and [b]Expeditions[/b], but for now this will suffice. 



Thank you so much, the future is bright.

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Game Director

FLAT28 Collective[/i]

[b]WELCOME TO LUNDONSTOCH[/b]
Hi Compeers!

Nice to meet you, we are the [b]FLAT28 Collective[/b].
FLAT28 is an international art collective consisting of [b]21 people [/b]spread across UK, America and Italy. We are Filmmakers, CGI Artists, Musicians, Cartoonists, Game Developers but most of all humans.
Last May we decided to embark on this journey, today we have a solid and tangible reality: A possible dream and a vertical slice.


[b]Glasshouse[/b] is first and foremost a classic role-playing game, but also a manifestation of existence, an intimate reflection on the world around us. The home of FLAT28 does not exist on common ground; it is a dreamlike instance that rests its foundation on numbers, codes and emotions.


FLAT28 is the virtual room that brought us together.
We hope Glasshouse will bind us to you as well.


[i]Until next time, FLAT28[/i]
